pr_title: ddl, types: fix int to datetime conversion to avoid useless retry
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #24839 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary: 

For the type conversion from `unsigned int` to `datetime`, a fundamental(unknown) error is returned.

The write reorganization stage of `ModifyColumn` uses `needRollbackData()` matching the error to detect whether the intermediate data should be cleaned:

```go
return kv.ErrKeyExists.Equal(err) || errCancelledDDLJob.Equal(err) || errCantDecodeRecord.Equal(err) ||
		types.ErrOverflow.Equal(err) || types.ErrDataTooLong.Equal(err) || types.ErrTruncated.Equal(err) ||
		json.ErrInvalidJSONText.Equal(err) || types.ErrBadNumber.Equal(err) || types.ErrInvalidYear.Equal(err) ||
		types.ErrWrongValue.Equal(err)
```

This is neither intuitive nor extendable. We should make it rollback **by default**, and explicitly define the errors that worth retrying instead.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

- Fix `unsigned int` -> `datetime` error message.
- Make `ModifyColumn` rollback by default.
- Add a simple test case.

### Related changes

NA

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test
- Integration test

Side effects

NA

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- No release note (since it is a sub-issue of "column type change" project)

issue_context.title: ddl: column type change will retry 512 time for error like `cannot convert datum from %s to type %s`
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
```sql
set @@tidb_enable_change_column_type=1;
drop table if exists t;
create table `t` (`a` int(10) unsigned default null);
insert into t values (1);
alter table t change column a b datetime;
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
give me a error as soon as possible

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
retry 512 times * 2.5 duration for 1pc sleep

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
master
